quiz.title: Module 2 — Tuesday — Audio Editing in CapCut
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers audio quality, syncing external audio, Mark Beats, cutting before the beat drops, keyframed volume, fades, Enhanced Voice, and the difference between J-cuts and L-cuts.

questions.prompt: Why does the instructor consider audio quality especially important when creating video content?
options: Audio quality eliminates the need for video editing.
Audio quality is only important for cinematic videos.
Poor audio can cause viewers to lose interest, even when the video quality is good.
Good audio automatically improves video resolution.
questions.explanation: Viewers will forgive a soft image far more readily than sound they have to strain to hear. Bad audio drives people away even when the picture is clean.

questions.prompt: Which CapCut feature allows an editor to synchronise external audio with video footage automatically?
options: Mark Beats
Sync Video to Sound
Enhanced Voice
Extract Audio
questions.explanation: Sync Video to Sound matches a separately recorded track to the picture, which saves hunting for the right offset by hand. Mark Beats, Enhanced Voice and Extract Audio all do other jobs.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of using the Mark Beats feature when editing music in CapCut?
options: To remove background noise from recorded audio.
To increase the volume of every music track.
To separate the audio from the video automatically.
To identify beats in a song so video clips can be aligned with the music.
questions.explanation: Mark Beats puts markers on the song's beats so you can snap cuts to them instead of guessing where the rhythm lands.

questions.prompt: According to the instructor, why might cutting a video one frame before a beat drops create a smoother viewing experience?
options: It can make the visual cut feel more naturally synchronised with the music.
It increases the video's frame rate automatically.
It prevents the music from playing during transitions.
It removes the need to edit the audio track.
questions.explanation: Because we see slightly before we hear, cutting a frame early lands the visual change right on the beat perceptually — the edit feels tighter than cutting exactly on it.

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of using keyframes to control music volume?
options: They automatically remove unwanted sounds from a recording.
They allow the editor to gradually change volume levels instead of creating abrupt transitions.
They synchronise all video clips with external microphones.
They convert background music into sound effects.
questions.explanation: Keyframes hold a volume value at a point in time, so setting two animates smoothly between them. That gives a gradual dip or lift instead of a jarring jump.

questions.prompt: What does applying a fade-in effect to an audio clip achieve?
options: It makes the audio start at full volume and stop immediately.
It removes the audio from the timeline.
It gradually increases the audio from a quieter level to its intended volume.
It automatically synchronises the audio with the video.
questions.explanation: A fade-in ramps the clip up from silence or a low level, so the sound arrives gently rather than starting abruptly.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of CapCut's Enhanced Voice feature, as explained in the tutorial?
options: To reduce background noise and improve voice clarity.
To add music markers to a soundtrack.
To create J-cuts and L-cuts automatically.
To increase the resolution of video footage.
questions.explanation: Enhanced Voice cleans up recorded speech, lifting the voice while pushing down noise so the dialogue sounds clearer.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a J-cut and an L-cut?
options: A J-cut changes video speed, while an L-cut changes audio pitch.
A J-cut removes the previous scene's audio, while an L-cut removes the next scene's audio.
A J-cut and an L-cut are both techniques for increasing music volume.
In a J-cut, the next scene's audio begins before its video appears; in an L-cut, the previous scene's audio continues after the video changes.
questions.explanation: The names describe the shape on the timeline. In a J-cut the incoming audio leads its picture; in an L-cut the outgoing audio trails behind its picture.
